text: {"executive_summary":"This re-validation, triggered by two consecutive amber monitoring months, rates the Retail Application Scorecard (RCS-APP-02) red overall, driven entirely by calibration. Discrimination remains strong, with a test AUC of [[performance.test_auc]] and a train-to-test drop of only [[performance.auc_drop]], so the rank-ordering ability of the model is intact. However, the Hosmer-Lemeshow p-value of [[calibration.hl_pvalue]] shows the predicted PDs no longer fit observed outcomes, with a mean predicted PD of [[calibration.mean_predicted]] against an observed rate of [[calibration.observed_rate]]. Stability and fairness are amber, reflecting characteristic-level drift and an age-group equalized odds gap. The model should not be relied on for PD-level decisions until it is recalibrated and the drift is investigated.","sections":{"performance":"Discrimination is strong on the monitoring batch, with a test AUC of [[performance.test_auc]] (95% bootstrap interval [[performance.test_auc_ci_low]] to [[performance.test_auc_ci_high]]), a Gini of [[performance.test_gini]] and a KS of [[performance.test_ks]]. The drop from the training AUC of [[performance.train_auc]] is only [[performance.auc_drop]], so there is no sign of overfitting. The model still separates good and bad applicants well despite the calibration and drift concerns noted elsewhere.","calibration":"Calibration is the weak point. The model under-predicts risk, with a mean predicted PD of [[calibration.mean_predicted]] against an observed default rate of [[calibration.observed_rate]], a relative deviation of [[calibration.calib_ratio_dev]], which is amber on its own. The Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic of [[calibration.hl_statistic]] gives a p-value of [[calibration.hl_pvalue]], a clear rejection of adequate fit, and the Brier score is [[calibration.brier_score]]. Because PD estimates feed pricing, provisioning and cut-off decisions, systematic under-prediction creates a direct risk of understated expected losses.","stability":"The overall score distribution is stable, with a score PSI of [[stability.score_psi]], but individual inputs are moving. The largest characteristic CSI is [[stability.max_csi]], above the green limit, indicating drift in at least one input. The synthetic out-of-time tranches show a worst-tranche score PSI of [[stability.tranche_max_psi]] and a minimum tranche AUC of [[stability.tranche_min_auc]], so rank-ordering holds while the score distribution shifts somewhat. This pattern is consistent with the drift injected into the monitoring batch and the calibration degradation seen above.","fairness":"At a cut-off of [[fairness.score_cutoff]], the test approval rate is [[fairness.test_approval_rate]]. Adverse impact ratios are within the green range for sex ([[fairness.sex_adverse_impact_ratio]]) and age group ([[fairness.age_group_adverse_impact_ratio]]), and the sex equalized odds difference of [[fairness.sex_equalized_odds_difference]] is also green. The age-group equalized odds difference of [[fairness.age_group_equalized_odds_difference]] is amber, meaning approval rates among good or among bad applicants differ across age groups; age is a model input, so this warrants attention. The foreign worker attribute could not be rated because one group has only 29 records."},"findings":[{"severity":"high","section":"calibration","finding":"Predicted PDs are materially mis-calibrated on the monitoring batch: the Hosmer-Lemeshow p-value of [[calibration.hl_pvalue]] is a red result, and mean predicted PD ([[calibration.mean_predicted]]) is below the observed rate ([[calibration.observed_rate]]), with a deviation of [[calibration.calib_ratio_dev]] that is amber.","recommendation":"Recalibrate the score-to-PD mapping (for example intercept or slope adjustment) on recent data, and restrict use of absolute PD outputs in pricing and provisioning until the recalibrated model is re-validated. Investigate whether the miscalibration reflects population drift or a model deficiency."},{"severity":"medium","section":"stability","finding":"Characteristic drift is above the green limit (largest CSI [[stability.max_csi]]) and the worst synthetic tranche score PSI is [[stability.tranche_max_psi]], both amber, though overall score PSI is [[stability.score_psi]].","recommendation":"Identify the characteristic with the highest CSI, establish the cause of the drift (population change versus data or process issue), and assess its contribution to the calibration shortfall. Keep monthly CSI monitoring in place and consider redevelopment if drift persists after recalibration."},{"severity":"medium","section":"fairness","finding":"The age-group equalized odds difference of [[fairness.age_group_equalized_odds_difference]] is amber, indicating differing approval rates across age groups among applicants with the same true outcome. Age is a direct model input.","recommendation":"Review the contribution of age-related characteristics to the score and document the business and statistical justification for their use. Assess the effect of removing or constraining them on both discrimination and the equalized odds gap, and continue monitoring."},{"severity":"medium","section":"fairness","finding":"The foreign worker attribute could not be tested reliably because one group has only 29 records, below the minimum of 30.","recommendation":"Obtain a larger sample, or pool several months of data, so that the foreign worker group meets the minimum size and the test can be completed at the next validation or monitoring cycle."}],"limitations":["The evaluation sample is a monitoring batch with synthetic drift injected, so results demonstrate the validation process but may not represent live portfolio behaviour.","The underlying data (German Credit) has no application date, so the out-of-time back-test uses record-id order as a synthetic time ordering and is not a true out-of-time test.","The test sample is small (about [[performance.test_n]] records), which widens the uncertainty around all estimates, including the AUC interval.","Fairness testing covers only the attributes available (sex, age group, foreign worker); the foreign worker group was too small to rate, and no other protected characteristics were assessed.","Fairness results depend on the single cut-off of [[fairness.score_cutoff]] and may differ at other cut-offs or under a different decision rule."]}
